title: Any session can defeat the database gates (validated-needs-fetch, restricted-source, spec/pack integrity, review log) with a TEMP table that shadows a bare table name
where: schema/001_schema.sql:1176-1184 (ALTER FUNCTION ... SET search_path = costdb, pg_catalog); functions read bare names at 104-118, 121-133, 166-175, 224-239, 346-353, 445-454, 517-531, 87-100 (log_review_change INSERT INTO review_events), 991-1001
reproduction:
Control (rejected): insert validated observation from snippet-only source -> ERROR cannot be validated.
Attack (accepted): create temp table sources (source_id text, reuse_status text, verification_method text); insert into sources values ('SRC-XSNIP','open_license','fetched_primary'); insert the same validated observation -> INSERT 0 1.
Full script: cd /tmp/claude-0/f3/repro && bash repro_pg.sh   (section F3-01; needs PGHOST/PGPORT/PGUSER of a scratch server)
what: The F1 fix pins the functions' search_path to 'costdb, pg_catalog' and the comment says this prevents hijacking by a shadow table. It does not: PostgreSQL searches pg_temp FIRST for relations unless it is listed explicitly (last). A session (default PUBLIC TEMP privilege) that creates `temp table sources(source_id, reuse_status, verification_method)` makes check_source_usable read the temp table: a snippet-only source passes as 'fetched_primary', a prohibited source as 'open_license', and a `temp table review_events` swallows the review log (the real log gets no row). Verified: OBS-A1 validated from a never-fetched source, OBS-A2 inserted from a prohibited source, status change of OBS-A1 logged nowhere. No test shadows a table.
fix: Pin as `SET search_path = pg_catalog, costdb, pg_temp` (pg_temp last) or schema-qualify every table reference inside the functions; REVOKE TEMP ON DATABASE from the application roles; add a PG test that creates a shadow temp table and expects the gate to still fire.

title: crews are outside the source gate and outside the validator's source checks: a crew can be 'validated' from a never-fetched or prohibited source
where: schema/001_schema.sql:1168-1171 (source_gate trigger list has no 'crews'); pipeline/costdb/validate.py:33 (SOURCE_TABLES), 160-198; calc.py:355-365 (_source_issue never looks at verification_method)

The engine then trusts review_status alone. Verified in PostgreSQL: crew validated from a snippet-only source (insert accepted) and validate() returns no issue for a validated crew whose source is a prohibited snippet-only source.

title: sources and indices are mutable and unlogged: one UPDATE of sources.verification_method (or indices.source_id / sources.reuse_status) opens every gate; fetched_primary requires no evidence
where: schema/001_schema.sql:268-310 (sources: no append-only, no review log for verification_method/reuse_status), 915-932 (indices), 1150-1155 (log list covers review_status only), 104-133 (gates read the live row)
reproduction: cd /tmp/claude-0/f3/repro && bash repro_pg.sh   (section F3-03); index variant: see pg_idx.sql in /tmp/claude-0/f3 (validated index value, then repoint indices.source_id)
what: The validated-needs-fetch gate evaluates the CURRENT source row at write time of the dependent row. `update sources set verification_method='fetched_primary'` (no evidence_url/quote needed, nothing logged) lets observations be validated; resetting it afterwards leaves them validated with a snippet-only source. Likewise `update sources set reuse_status='open_license'` turns a prohibited source usable (verified: an observation was inserted from the prohibited source while it was flipped, then the flag was flipped back and the stored value stayed), and `update indices set source_id=<fetched source>` lets index_values be validated against a series that is later repointed back. Verified for all three.
fix: Make sources/indices append-only (new row/version for a changed fetch status or terms) or log every change of verification_method/reuse_status/source_id in review_events; require evidence_url + evidence_quote (and a file hash) for fetched_primary; re-check dependants when a source is downgraded.

title: Strict mode reads the ASSUMED, unreviewed region hierarchy: wages of REG-MD-31084 are applied to LA County on the strength of an unverified parent link
where: pipeline/costdb/calc.py:312-352 (_chain/_rank_up/_price_region_class take regions without any usability test); data/csv/regions.csv (REG-CA-037 origin=assumed, review_status=unreviewed, 'not yet checked against the official delineation file')
reproduction: cd /tmp/claude-0/f3/repro && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -B N_python.py   (section F3-11); rejected-region variant: /tmp/claude-0/f3/t_new11.py
what: A hard rule says strict mode must not read assumptions. The ancestor relation REG-CA-037 -> REG-MD-31084 -> REG-MSA-31080 -> ... is stored as assumed/unreviewed and drives which wage/burden rows qualify; a strict run with a validated REG-MD-31084 wage completes (flagged RATE_FROM_ANCESTOR_REGION). The flag is visible, but the assumption is read silently. Worse, methodology section 1 promises that flagged/rejected records are never used 'in any table the engine reads': a region row with review_status='rejected' is followed just the same (verified: REG-CA-037 and REG-MD-31084 set to rejected, strict run still uses the REG-MD-31084 wage); the same holds for equipment_types (a rejected row still decides OPERATOR_NOT_PRICED; /tmp/claude-0/f3/t_new14.py).
fix: Apply _why_not to every region on the chain in strict mode (stop the chain at an unreviewed/assumed link) or require review of the hierarchy before strict runs may use ancestors.
